title: System programming — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: Deliberately not a Go/Rust-std system library. The primitives it exposes — managed child processes, environment, working directory, filesystem, monotonic clocks, a libuv reactor — are a clean but intentional subset of what those stdlibs and libuv carry. What it adds that none of them have is the layer above: an in-memory rehearsal twin over files, env and spawns, a single narrated / scoped / audited `stzUpdatePlan` that is the only bridge to reality, and a capability-actor lattice where an inference-only (LLM) actor's effect set is empty by construction — "agents that cannot hurt you," enforced in code. On top sits a complete delivery plane. It omits by design what a governed-effects surface doesn't need: signals, broad IPC, the raw syscall zoo.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Read the shape honestly: one category-leading strength (governance), a broad band of solid-but-subset OS basics, and a few deliberate omissions.

lanes.engine: One closed capability lattice (`effectful/sensing/compute/inference` + postures) in `stzSystemActor`; a rehearsal twin (`stzVirtualSystem` / `stzVirtualFileSystem` / `stzVirtualEnvironment`) that touches nothing; and `stzUpdatePlan` — the sole crossing — which commits only through three gates (reject · scope · governance). An LLM actor's effect set is empty, so it commits nothing, in every domain.
lanes.owed: No stdlib has any of this — it is the substrate the agentic safe-world binding rides on. Proven: a queued spawn does not run until commit (marker-file verified); scope refusals never reach disk. A genuine category-of-one.

lanes.engine: Managed children (`system.zig`): `Spawn`, streaming `ReadOutput`/`ReadError`, `Wait`, `ExitCode`, `Kill`, no-leak `Close` — plus a `SystemCall` front whose double-exec bug is fixed (one spawn returns `[stdout, exit, stderr]`).
lanes.owed: `ExePath`, `IsAlive` and a process table are named but have no Ring consumer yet; no pty. The common lifecycle is clean and leak-safe.

lanes.engine: Get / set / unset / list env vars, cwd get/set, hostname, username, cpu-count — engine-backed. On Windows, a set value uses `SetEnvironmentVariableW` so later child spawns inherit it.
lanes.owed: Complete for the everyday surface, and correctly wired to child inheritance. Nothing structural owed.

lanes.engine: `file.zig`: read / write / append / copy / delete / stat, and dir create / delete / list / walk / count — path args screened by `pathIsUsable`. The rehearsal twin adds governed create/write/copy/move over the same primitives.
lanes.owed: Covers the common ops (and adds a twin no stdlib has) — but omits permissions, ownership, symlinks and fifos that Go/Rust std carry (see lane 11).

lanes.engine: OS / arch / endianness / pointer-size / bit-size, cpu-count, machine memory (total/free) and process memory (RSS/peak/CPU-time), with declared profiles that model non-host targets (rtos/android/esp32). Discipline: "facts are engine, opinions are Ring" — the old Ring `getarch()` was retired.
lanes.owed: Solid machine/process facts with no double source — but not a deep sysinfo (no per-disk, per-NIC, load average or thermals).

lanes.engine: `time.zig`: monotonic ns/us/ms, wall UTC, sleep, and clock resolution — with process uptime taken from a monotonic base instant captured at DLL load (the old epoch-uptime bug is fixed and guarded).
lanes.owed: Monotonic-vs-wall is correctly separated (a real correctness win). Calendar / timezone time is the datetime module's, by design.

lanes.engine: A governed define → require → feasibility → plan → execute → ship pipeline in one vocabulary: `stzDeployment` + `stzDeploymentSite` with a step DAG, rollback and provisioning. `Deploy(:Production)` is real and gated (`MayCommit` = actor holds `effectful`); a bare call touches nothing. Git and LocalRepo backends proven byte-for-byte.
lanes.owed: Server (scp/ssh), Registry (docker) and Device (flash) backends generate correct commands but are not yet live-verified against a real host / account — "one reachable host away from literal."

lanes.engine: `stzBuilder` + `build.zig wasm` produce a bundle; `stzEmulator` gives `Deploy(:Emulated)` a rehearsed run; `stzWebBundle` packages the WASM edge; `stzPlatform` drives Build→Deploy (refusing to deploy what wasn't built).
lanes.owed: A real build+emulate stage feeding the deploy plane — focused on Softanza's own artifacts (WASM edge, deployable bundles), not a general build tool.

lanes.engine: `reactor.zig` is a libuv-backed cross-platform event loop (epoll / kqueue / IOCP), but in this group only its first slice ships — `version` + `selftest`.
lanes.owed: The full async multiplexing surface is the Concurrency & distribution plane's, and only its first slice is here. No thread-spawn API in the system group (`threads` is a lattice token, not a call).

lanes.engine: Path helpers (extension / basename / dirname) and the common file/dir ops ship; a coarse engine sandbox flag (`stz_config_sandbox`) is designed as a belt-and-braces companion to the twin.
lanes.owed: Deliberately omitted: file permissions / ownership / symlinks / fifos, mmap, users/groups, ptrace, raw syscalls. A focused governed surface, not an `os`/`syscall` clone.

lanes.engine: Inter-process communication is the managed child's stdout / stderr / stdin pipes — enough to drive and read a subprocess.
lanes.owed: No named pipes, shared memory or socketpair IPC. Cross-process coordination beyond parent↔child stdio is not a lane yet (sockets are the network module's).

lanes.engine: None. There is no signal handling — `grep` finds no `stz_signal*` in the engine and no Ring signal class.
lanes.owed: No SIGINT / SIGTERM / SIGCHLD handling — so no graceful shutdown, no child-reaping on signal, no Ctrl-C hook. A real gap for a system-programming surface.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first closes the two most load-bearing omissions for real system work; the second finishes named-but-unbuilt pieces; the third is the OS breadth this surface leaves to the stdlibs on purpose.

items.title: Signal handling
items.text: SIGINT / SIGTERM / SIGCHLD (and the Windows console-control equivalents) — the difference between a process that can shut down gracefully and reap its children and one that can't. Absent today, and essential for anything long-running.

items.title: The full async reactor surface
items.text: Only the reactor's first slice ships here; real async multiplexing (timers, I/O, tasks) is the Concurrency & distribution plane's — and it is what most I/O-bound system work needs. Landing it turns a governed effects surface into a governed runtime.

tiers.title: Tier B — finish the named pieces

items.title: Complete the process face
items.text: `ExePath`, `IsAlive` and the process table (`proc_list`/`proc_exists`) are named but have no Ring consumer. Small additions over the existing engine surface.

items.title: Live-verify the deploy backends
items.text: Server (ssh/scp), Registry (docker) and Device (flash) generate correct commands but aren't run against a real host/account. Proving one of each end-to-end makes "one host away from literal" actually literal.

items.title: Unify SystemCall over Spawn
items.text: Re-express `stzSystemCall` over `stzProcess.Spawn` so there is one spawn implementation, not two. The double-exec fix already landed; this removes the remaining parallel path.

tiers.title: Tier C — OS breadth, on demand

items.title: The lower OS surface
items.text: File permissions / ownership / symlinks, users/groups, and the metadata the stdlibs carry — added where a real workload needs them, keeping the governed-effects framing rather than cloning `os`/`syscall` wholesale.

items.title: Richer IPC
items.text: Named pipes, shared memory and socketpair beyond child stdio — the cross-process coordination a multi-process app eventually needs, ideally as governed operations under the twin.

items.title: The engine sandbox flag
items.text: Wire the designed coarse `stz_config_sandbox` as the belt-and-braces companion to the twin — a hard engine-level backstop under the soft governance gate, so even a bug in Ring can't cross to reality.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main`. Heavily guarded (~335 assertions across eight+ guards) proving exactly the distinctive parts: uptime is monotonic seconds not epoch (the fix), SystemCall is a single spawn (the double-exec fix), a queued spawn does not run until commit (marker-file verified), an LLM empty-effect actor commits nothing across files and env, and out-of-scope operations never reach disk. One test errors (`test_system_engine2.ring` — a stale engine binding). The deploy plane's Git/LocalRepo backends are proven end-to-end; ssh/aws/registry/device are command-generated and infra-gated.

Softanza's system layer is not trying to out-surface Go or Rust — it exposes a deliberate subset of OS primitives and wraps them in the one thing those stdlibs lack: a rehearse-then-commit, capability-gated bridge to reality where an LLM cannot act by construction; its gaps are the classic OS pieces (signals, IPC, full async, the lower syscall surface) it will add as real workloads earn them.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-16, from a read-only `main` worktree — Ring faces under `base/system` (`stzProcess`, `stzSystemCall`, `stzEnvironment`, `stzSystemActor`, `stzVirtualFileSystem`, `stzVirtualSystem`, `stzUpdatePlan`, `stzDelivery`/`stzDeployment`) and `base/platform`; engine `system.zig`, `process.zig`, `file.zig`, `time.zig`, `perf.zig`, `reactor.zig`; plan of record `SOFTANZA_SYSTEM_FOUNDATION.md` + `SOFTANZA_DELIVERY_PLANE.md`; guards under `test/system` + `test/platform` (~335 asserts). Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
